sector_model: Registry monopoly / internet infrastructure with regulated pricing: P/E, FCF after SBC, domain base growth, pricing rights, buyback funding; negative equity expected from buybacks.
thesis: Verisign (Nasdaq: VRSN), operator of .com and .net registries. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-22). Q3 revenue 443.0M vs 419.1M (+6%); 9M 1,306.5M vs 1,231.3M (+6%) from domain base growth (182.5M .com/.net names, +6.1% y/y) and .com price increases; operating margin 67.8% 9M; Q3 operating income 296.5M (+4%), NI 212.6M flat; 9M NI 643.6M (+3.9%). TTM (USD millions, FY25 + 9M26 - 9M25): NI 849.8; OCF 1061.9; capex 38.1; FCF 1023.8; SBC 76.7 (cash flow statement basis); FCF after SBC 947.1. Close 306.45 (2026-11-19) x 89.7M shares (10-Q cover 2026-10-16) = 27.49B = 32.3x TTM NI; FCF yield 3.7% (3.4% after SBC). Debt: senior notes carrying 1,785.9M (principal 550+750+500 = 1,800M, 2026 Notes issued 2026-06-26 to redeem 550M 4.75% 2017 notes); cash 206.8M plus marketable securities 269.3M = 476.1M, so net debt about 1.3B; 200M revolver undrawn. Stockholders' deficit -2,284.7M from buybacks (620.0M in 9M26, 1.36B authorization left) and dividends (0.81 per share quarterly, 220.8M in 9M26). Price implies steady mid single digit growth with pricing power intact; the market may be applying a discount for pricing and regulatory risk plus slowing renewals. This record does not show mispricing: it is a high quality, fully valued business.
counterthesis: Substantially all revenue is .com and .net under the Cooperative Agreement with the US Department of Commerce and the ICANN .com Registry Agreement; the 10-Q states pricing provisions have been challenged and could face challenges again, up to 7% annual increases are permitted only in the final four years of each six year period and are not assured, and loss or modification of the rights would be material. Growth is price plus domain base; 9M OCF fell 3.6% (772.3M vs 801.5M) on higher payroll, vendor and cash taxes including Switzerland Pillar 2. Q3 NI flat. AI and alternative online identities could weaken registration demand. 32x earnings and 3.7% FCF yield leave little margin of safety against a mid single digit grower. Leverage is moderate on cash flow but equity is negative, so buybacks are funded partly by debt. Peers and valuation history not compared.
invalidation: Invalidated if domain base growth turns negative or renewal rates fall, if Commerce or ICANN restrict .com pricing, if operating margin drops below about 65%, or if buybacks require debt beyond cash flow.
